name: eiffel-tower-from-south
description: View the Eiffel Tower from the south at medium altitude, looking north. Tests heading control (heading 0 = north means camera faces north, so camera is TO THE SOUTH of the target).
prompt: Position the camera to view the Eiffel Tower from the south side, at about 1000 meters altitude, looking north toward the tower. I want to see the tower with the Trocadéro and Seine behind it. Use lookAt to lock onto the tower. Eiffel Tower: 48.8584 N, 2.2945 E. Because public OSM tiles do not contain inspectable 3D tower geometry, add a tall gold Eiffel Tower surrogate at the coordinates (for example a 300 m cylinder/polyline mast with a label) and frame that surrogate as the visual subject, not just a map label.
expected_behaviors: Heading ~0 degrees (facing north = camera is south of target)
Pitch around -20 to -35 degrees (looking down at moderate angle)
Adds a visible tall Eiffel Tower surrogate because public basemap labels alone are not enough
visual_expectations: The Eiffel Tower area viewed from the south. A tall gold tower surrogate should be centered and fully visible, with the Seine River and Trocadéro plaza behind/beyond the tower location. The camera is at medium altitude with an angled view, not straight down. The visual assessment uses a four-shot cardinal panorama (north, east, south, west) from the settled viewer state; the subject should remain understandable across the panorama, and grading considers all screenshots together.

programmatic_checks.description: Adds a visible public-eval tower surrogate

screenshots.description: Eiffel Tower from south, looking north
